label: alg:mass-identity
title: Nucleon mass ratio $m_p = 2\,(m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 6 m_e) \cdot R_{\mathrm{s5bb}}$ (muon-anchored Hecke energy)
html:
Algorithm (Nucleon mass ratio at q = q_0).

The name mass identity is deliberately not used here. It is already taken by def:mass-identity, which is a different object — inertial mass as a nonabelian multiplicative integral around a vortex filament. This step computes the dimensionless nucleon ratio from the muon-anchored Hecke energy. Evaluate the nucleon mass ratio via the muon-anchored Hecke energy — the form adopted here as canonical. Absolute nucleon mass in MeV is not a framework prediction: m_e sets the MeV scale by fiat, so the predictive content is the dimensionless ratio m_p/m_e; the MeV outputs below are that ratio rendered against the m_e unit, a rendering rather than an independent absolute-mass claim.

m_p = \dim V_{(2,1)} \cdot \bigl( m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - |S_3| \cdot m_e \bigr), \qquad
m_\mu = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) / \hbar_q^2 ,

with the dimensionless Hecke factor F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| \cdot [3]_q! / q^3, via the canonical chain Steps 1 \to 3 \to 5 \to here. This is the raw identity: the substrate parameter q_0 is pinned by solving exactly this form against m_p/m_e (an earlier version of the pin carried a fitted Habiro 4-loop dressing, which is not used here), so the identity round-trips m_p by construction and m_\mu, m_n are the predictions.

Fit-tier dressing (not canonical). An optional 4-loop factor R_{\mathrm{s5bb}} = (1 + c_4 u^4)(1 + 4 u^5)(1 - 29 u^6), u = b\,\hbar_q^2, b = \sqrt{(q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^2}, is retained in the producer (m_p_substrate_identity_50dps.habiro_ratio_s5bb) but is fit-tier, not derived: the exact c_4 that lands m_p on CODATA is linear in the q_0 pin offset (so c_4 merely reparametrizes the \mu–p tension), and neither c_4 = 46 nor c_4 = 4143/90 is derived anywhere in this paper. Applied at the raw pin it overshoots CODATA m_p by \approx 242 ppb. Which value to adopt — or whether to drop the dressing altogether — is unresolved.

Input

  • Substrate parameter q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{> 1} (CAL-2 anchor; phys-obs layer pins on m_p/m_e).
  • Electron mass m_e in MeV (CAL-1 anchor).
  • \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299 (figure-eight knot, Lobachevsky closed form 6\Lambda(\pi/3) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3): two regular ideal tetrahedra, each of volume \Lambda(\alpha)+\Lambda(\beta)+\Lambda(\gamma) at \alpha=\beta=\gamma=\pi/3 [martelli2016] (Thm.~13.1.3, Cor.~13.1.4); the muon's knot).

Output

  • Mass ratios m_p/m_e, m_n/m_e, rendered against the m_e scale as m_p, m_n \in \mathbb{R}_{> 0} in MeV (the MeV figure is a rendering of the dimensionless ratio, not an absolute-mass prediction).

Algorithm

1. Compute |tr_M(β_Bor, q)| = (4 + h² − 3h⁴ − h⁶)/(h² + 4)
   (Lean-proved closed form, BorromeanMarkovTrace.lean; h = q − q⁻¹).
2. Form F_Bor = |tr_M(β_Bor)| · [3]_q! / q³   ([3]_q! Lean-proved).
3. Muon anchor: m_μ = m_e · Vol(4₁) / ℏ_q²  (ℏ_q = 1 − q⁻¹).
4. m_p = 2·(m_μ·F_Bor − 6·m_e)   (raw identity; no habiro dressing).
5. m_n = m_p + Q_β + m_e with the parameter-free Kashiwara b²
   truncation Q_β (derived_masses.q_beta_kashiwara_n2_mev).
6. Evaluate at q = q₀ with 50-dps mpmath precision.

Correctness conditions

  1. prop:mass-identity-exists gives existence of the nucleon mass ratio in the QOU premise.
  2. prop:mass-identity-unique makes the identity unique modulo the calibration choice.
  3. thm:knot-mass-formula-unified ties the categorical scalar to the archimedean MeV observable.

Complexity

Closed-form throughout (no Hecke machinery needed): sub-millisecond at 50 dps.

Python API entry point

from canonical_mass import proton_neutron_mass_mev

m_p_MeV, m_n_MeV = proton_neutron_mass_mev()

computations/canonical_mass.py is the single entry point: it prefers the producer witness and falls back to the raw identity above (no R_{\mathrm{s5bb}} dressing — the fallback matches the raw pin). Producer: m_p_substrate_identity_50dps.py.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: m-p-substrate-identity-50dps.witness.json (predictions m_p, m_n, m_\mu, CODATA anchors, ppb residuals). Residuals for this and the other observables are collected in per-observable-100x-status.witness.json.

Notes

Superseded forms: the volume-density expressions m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \lambda_A / \hbar_q^2 (\approx 966 MeV, a CODATA-implied fit) and m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M / \hbar_q^2 (\approx 406 MeV) are NOT the absolute nucleon mass; the old "+2.89 % m_p gap" was the \lambda_A fit artifact. vol_density_per_block remains valid for binding ratios only (the scale cancels) — the binding-side per-knot density is Step 9b's \Delta_\lambda frontier.

Anchor bookkeeping: at the proton-pinned q_0 the m_p value is an anchor round-trip (exact in ratio space), m_\mu and m_n are the predictions; the pin's Habiro dressing reconciles the muon identity to \approx 1.4 ppb (the c_4 discrepancy between the pin and the producer, 46 versus 4143/90, is unresolved).

Linking-weight selection rule (binding-side, retained for Step 9b): the factor \mathrm{lw}(c) = \frac{1}{c+1}\sum_{\lambda \vdash c+1} \dim_q V_\lambda reproduces \mathrm{lw}(1)=1 (muon) and \mathrm{lw}(3) = (3q^2+4+3q^{-2})/4 (Family-A — bit-for-bit equal to linking_weight_family_a, now deprecated for absolute mass), and gives \mathrm{lw}(2) = (q+1)^2/(3q) (prop:selection-rule-c2-prediction). Regression-tied to production by binding_selection_rule_tau_closure.py \to witness. The same \mathrm{lw}(c) values are the SW-period anchors of the depth-2 binding kernel — see mba-step09b.
